_comment: Source of truth for what is published at https://vizora.cloud/tv and
https://vizora.cloud/downloads/vizora-display.apk.
`candidate` is the artifact verified by scripts/release/verify-display-apk.mjs.
`published` is the artifact currently live (null until the first publish); it is
the baseline the next release's signing certificate and versionCode are compared
against.
`approval` encodes the two release gates. publish-display-apk.sh REFUSES to run
while either pair is null. Do not fill these in without the named human actually
confirming. Never put the keystore, its password, or any private key in this repo.
The canonical Vizora Android customer-signing identity.
Every publish — INCLUDING THE FIRST — must produce an APK whose signing
certificate equals canonicalCertSha256. The `published` baseline below only
protects release 2 onward; pinning here is what protects release 1, which is
exactly where the 2026-08-10 mismatch was found.
Pin this ONLY after the key passes full durability verification: private-key
entry exists, certificate SHA-256 known, keystore has a secure off-machine
backup, credentials recoverable by an authorized operator, and restoration
tested well enough to prove the key still signs. Record classification and
ownership only — never a password or private-key material.
signing.backupClass: encrypted (aes-256-cbc/pbkdf2) copy on the company VPS at /opt/secure-backups/vizora/android-signing — dir 700, file 600, root-owned, outside every web, Docker and application root; credentials held separately in an owner-controlled password manager
_findings_2026_08_10: GATE B FAILED. The key that signed vizora-display-1.3.10-release.apk
(cert AA07524A…A5137982, created 2026-03-31) is NOT on the Windows build
machine. The only Android keystore there — vizora-tv android/vizora-release.jks,
single entry, alias vizora-display, created 2026-03-26 — carries a DIFFERENT
certificate: BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Not signed in CI, not the debug key, and no
other .jks/.keystore exists under the user profile or OneDrive.
DO NOT PUBLISH the existing 1.3.10 APK. Once canonicalCertSha256 is pinned to
a durable key, the verifier refuses that binary automatically — its cert will
_status_2026_08_10_evening: 1.3.11 has now been BUILT and fully verified against the on-machine key,
and its certificate is BE2320A5…3A9187A5 — matching the rehearsal candidate
exactly, which independently confirms which key actually signs here.
GATE B IS STILL FAILED, and it is the only thing between this build and
publication. Its two open items are facts about custody, not paperwork:
- no secure OFF-MACHINE backup of the keystore
- no credential recovery independent of this one Windows machine
Neither can be closed by an agent, because neither is a decision — they
require someone to actually place the backup and own the recovery.
Publishing before they are closed is the one irreversible move here: the
risk starts the moment a customer installs, and if the key is then lost
every TV in the field needs uninstall + re-pair to ever update again.
_playStoreNote: Before customer rollout, compare the canonical sideload certificate with the
Google Play App Signing certificate. If they differ, pilot customers migrating
from the sideloaded APK to the Play Store build will need one uninstall +
reinstall (and will re-pair). Document it before the migration, not after.

_comment: LIVE at https://vizora.cloud/tv and /downloads/vizora-display.apk since 2026-08-11.
Published bytes verified against this hash from the server and from an independent
network; the /tv page asserts the same version and hash.
Screen-sleep fix. Installed as an UPDATE over 1.3.11 (same certificate,
versionCode 10142 > 10141), so paired screens kept their pairing.
Hardware acceptance is POST-PUBLICATION: the first customer installation is the
test. See approval._gateA_scope.
This block is the baseline the NEXT release is compared against: its signing
certificate must match, and versionCode must be strictly greater than 10142.

approval._gateA: Artifact approval — confirm this exact APK is the intended client-pilot build, not merely the newest GitHub prerelease.
_gateA_scope: APPROVED 2026-08-11, bound to apkSha256
1D035BDBB48720B9BCE1F0C8ADA8E74436E9D37A03D9A11FF7CEFA6B515F8EF7 and nothing else.
Android release builds are not byte-reproducible, so a rebuild — even from the same
commit — produces a different binary and VOIDS this approval. Reset to null and
re-approve if that ever happens.
POST-PUBLICATION PILOT CONFIRMATION — REQUIRED
Publication is distribution-only and does not update existing Android TV
installations. The TV client has NO auto-update path: its command set is
push_content / reload / clear_cache / unpair / update_config plus content types,
none of which installs an APK (electron-updater belongs to the desktop client and
is untouched). Screens already on 1.3.11 stay there unless someone deliberately
installs. That is why this approval could move from pre-publication acceptance to
post-publication confirmation without widening the blast radius: in this window the
only installer is the pilot customer.
Gate A was therefore approved on source, static and binary evidence for a bounded
one-customer pilot. THE FIRST CUSTOMER INSTALLATION IS THE HARDWARE ACCEPTANCE TEST
for screen-awake behaviour.
Outcomes:
- Panel stays awake past its configured timeout -> close the defect.
- Flag present but panel still sleeps -> reopen the OEM POWER-POLICY question
only, NOT this application-layer implementation. FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON cannot
reach an OEM eco/no-signal mode. Do not add WakeLocks speculatively.
Customer instruction: install from vizora.cloud/tv OVER the existing app. Do not
uninstall first — uninstalling wipes app data and forces re-pairing.
Caveat worth knowing: we cannot confirm server-side which build a screen runs.
The TV sends appVersion in every heartbeat, but the gateway never reads it and
nothing writes it to Display.metadata (0 of 23 prod devices have the key), while
the dashboard renders an App Version row that can never populate. Tracked as TV2.
UPDATE 2026-08-11: TV2 is fixed — the heartbeat appVersion is now persisted to
devices.metadata, so future rollouts can be confirmed server-side rather than by asking
the customer. The caveat above stood at the time 1.3.12 was approved.
approval._gateB: Signing-key durability — confirm the release keystore has a secure off-machine backup and a recoverable password owned by an authorized operator. Record location CLASS and ownership only, never the key or password.
_gateB_evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-10 (second attempt). Split by who established what, so a future
reader knows which parts are machine-checked and which rest on the owner.
Machine-verified: the encrypted backup was created, uploaded, then RETRIEVED
FROM THE VPS and restored — decrypt produced a file byte-identical to the
original (DB5C23DD…654BC3), which opened as PrivateKeyEntry alias
vizora-display and signed a disposable APK that apksigner verified across
v1+v2+v3 with certificate BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Isolation verified, not assumed:
no nginx root/alias into /opt, no container mount, 4/4 HTTP probes 404. The
original keystore re-hashed unchanged and every temporary copy was shredded.
Ciphertext on the VPS: A666578E…98A725F3, 600, root-owned.
Owner-attested (not machine-checkable, by design): both secrets — the backup
encryption passphrase and the keystore password — were filed in an
owner-controlled password manager and read back before the staging folder was
deleted. Confirmed by Srini 2026-08-10; the deletion was independently
re-checked here and no stray copy remains on the build machine.
Recovery after a total build-machine loss: vault -> passphrase -> decrypt the
VPS copy -> vault -> keystore password -> open. No step depends on the Windows
machine, which is what this gate exists to guarantee.
PRIOR INCIDENT, kept deliberately: this gate was closed and reopened earlier
the same day because the first passphrase was lost, making the first ciphertext
permanently undecryptable. The key was never at risk. The cause was ordering —
the staging folder was deleted before read-back from the vault was confirmed.
Filing a secret is not the same as having it. Re-run the restore drill
periodically; key custody rots quietly and only surfaces when it is expensive.
approval.signingKeyLocationClass: encrypted copy on company VPS outside all web/app roots + credentials in an owner-controlled password manager
